description: Welcome to Vitarix! We are a team of enthusiastic and creative individuals passionate about technology, innovation, and space exploration. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to develop an innovative health-monitoring software solution to support astronauts during space missions. We believe in teamwork, creative thinking, and turning ideas into meaningful solutions. We welcome curious minds, passionate learners, and innovative thinkers who are excited to collaborate, share knowledge..
summary: VITARIX is a web-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to support astronaut health and well-being during space missions. It provides a centralized platform to record and monitor physical and mental health information, assess potential health risks, track sleep patterns, and maintain health records. The system also provides wellness recommendations and information about major spaceflight hazards, helping users understand their possible effects on astronaut health. Through an interactive dashboard, health check-ins, visual analytics, and report generation, VITARIX makes health information easier to access and understand. The project aims to support continuous health awareness and organized health monitoring, particularly during long-duration space missions.
details:
VITARIX is a web-based astronaut health monitoring system developed to support health awareness during space missions. It provides an interactive dashboard where health information can be entered, viewed, and monitored through different modules.

The system includes astronaut profiles, health check-ins, risk assessment, physical and mental health records, sleep monitoring, wellness recommendations, and spaceflight hazard awareness. It presents health information through visual charts and an interactive body model. Users can also generate health reports to review recorded information.

VITARIX is developed using Python and Flask for backend processing, SQLite for database management, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend. Chart.js is used for data visualization.

The project considers important spaceflight challenges such as radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile environments. Its aim is to make astronaut health information easier to organize, understand, and review, especially during long-duration missions.

VITARIX is currently a software-based demonstration that uses manually entered health information. It does not directly connect to spacecraft sensors or provide medical diagnoses.
